wave: SECURITY / SEMANTIC PRESERVATION -- OwnershipIdentity::identity_key() joined `name` into the identity string with a bare, unescaped `|` delimiter, even though `name` is not always a bare identifier: for a borrow whose referent is not a single path (`&(a | b)`, `&foo()`, any non-Path expression), the extractor sets `name` to that expression's raw token-stream spelling, which is not filtered through any restrictive lexer and can genuinely contain `|`.

gap_discovered_by: Delegated Explore subagent survey, explicitly scoped to files not yet reviewed this session, cross-checking every sibling dimension's identity struct for the same unescaped-join risk. It found OwnershipIdentity.name is the ONLY dimension among Call/ControlFlow/DataFlow/State/Effect/Ownership/Concurrency/Persistence whose free-text field is not always a bare `syn::Ident` (StateAccessIdentity/ValueIdentity's `name` fields are always bare identifiers, `|`-free by construction; EffectIdentity/PersistenceIdentity/ConcurrencyIdentity carry no free-text field at all). Its finding was independently re-verified before any change: read `adapter/src/semantic/rust/ownership.rs`'s real walker directly (confirmed `call_callee_spelling` falls back to `other.to_token_stream().to_string()` for any non-Path referent, with no charset restriction), read `core/src/semantic/ownership.rs`'s real `identity_key()` directly (confirmed the bare `|`-join, unescaped), read `core/src/identity/mod.rs`'s `escape_identity_field` doc comment directly (confirmed it explicitly names this exact class: 'a field extracted through a real lexer that forbids separator in a valid token... doesn't [need escaping]' vs. this field, which is NOT always extracted that way), and independently constructed and ran a concrete byte-identical collision against the real, unfixed implementation before writing any fix.
key_finding: core/src/semantic/ownership.rs::OwnershipIdentity::identity_key() joins `name` via a bare `|` with no escaping. `adapter/src/semantic/rust/ownership.rs`'s `Expr::Reference` arm sets `name = call_callee_spelling(&reference.expr)`, and for any referent that is not a bare single-segment path, `call_callee_spelling` falls back to `other.to_token_stream().to_string()` -- the raw pretty-printed source text, which can contain `|` (a bitwise-OR expression, a match-pattern-like construct inside a macro, a string/char literal containing `|`, etc.) with no lexer restricting it. Two structurally distinct OwnershipIdentity values -- `{name: "a", span.path: "b|1:2|BORROW_MUT", line: 3, col: 4, kind: BorrowShared}` and `{name: "a|b|1:2", span.path: "BORROW_MUT", line: 3, col: 4, kind: BorrowShared}` -- render to the byte-identical string `...|a|b|1:2|BORROW_MUT:3:4|BORROW_SHARED`, confirmed by direct execution against the real, unfixed code. `record_dimension_hit` (adapter/src/semantic/rust/mod.rs) dedups purely by the string derived from this identity, so the second of two such colliding sites is silently dropped: no observation, no evidence record, and the census undercounts real ownership operations with no diagnostic.

design_decisions.question: Escape only `name`, or also `span.path` (which the survey also flagged as theoretically joinable)?
design_decisions.decision: Escape only `name`, matching this codebase's own consistent, already-established precedent: no identity_key() anywhere in the workspace (CallSiteIdentity, StateAccessIdentity, ValueIdentity, PersistenceIdentity, ConcurrencyIdentity, DependencyIdentity, the ADL/graph fixes from earlier this session) escapes `span.path` or any other path-shaped field -- file paths come from a real repository walk, not a permissive text parser, and the codebase treats that as out of scope everywhere else. Escaping `name` alone is also PROVABLY sufficient: once `name` cannot contain a raw (unescaped) `|`, the first unescaped `|` after it in the joined string is an unambiguous boundary, so two different escaped names can never render an identical prefix, and the remaining tail fields (path/line/col/kind) were never the source of the actual defect.

design_decisions.question: How to falsify before trusting the fix?
design_decisions.decision: Constructed a concrete byte-identical collision pair by hand (not a hypothetical), added it as a test, confirmed it FAILS (both sides produce the same string) against the real unfixed identity_key(), then applied the escaping fix and confirmed the same test passes -- directly demonstrating both that the defect was real and that the fix closes it, rather than relying on the survey's own unverified confidence claim.
